name: Urban Suite - Pollution
miniText: The scientific question is whether pollution diffusion and local mitigation alter population persistence. In NetLogo's Urban Suite - Pollution model, power plants maintain pollutant sources, trees reduce nearby pollution and moving people lose health or reproduce depending on their condition. The selected literature connects this mechanism to coupled environmental stress and demographic feedback: toxicant-population models formalize exposure-dependent persistence and extinction [1]; coupled population dynamics supply a classical ecological comparison [2]; embodied ecological models clarify links between individual rules and population outcomes [3]. Pollution is an abstract field, and health decline is a stipulated exposure rule; tree effects are not calibrated removal rates or epidemiological risk estimates. The original NetLogo behavior is the baseline for reimplementation. This simulation offers a controlled thought experiment, and agreement with its output does not establish empirical validation.

modelSource.scientificOrigin: The original version of this model was developed during the Sprawl/Swarm Class at Illinois Institute of Technology in Fall 2006 under the supervision of Sarah Dunn and Martin Felsen, by the following student: Young Jang. See http://www.sprawlcity.us/ for more information about the course. Further modifications and refinements on the model were made by members of the Center for Connected Learning and Computer-Based Modeling before its release as an Urban Suite model. The Urban Suite models were developed as part of the Procedural Modeling of Cities project, under the sponsorship of NSF ITR award 0326542, Electronic Arts & Maxis. Please see the project web site ( http://ccl.northwestern.edu/cities/ ) for more information.
modelSource.notes: This is source research, not runtime execution or approval of the City Library reimplementation. Original model notices remain in the retained source.
